title: risk-aware-pilot-casebook-and-pricing-playbook-2027
author: Olivia Martinez
content:
Overview
--------
This document is a compact, sales-facing playbook for engaging risk-sensitive prospects (finance, healthcare, regulated SaaS) who require an evidence-led pilot and clear pricing guardrails. It bundles: value positioning, a distilled competitive brief, a one-page pitch-deck outline, pricing templates for pilot and scale, two anonymized case studies, a short security FAQ tailored to procurement/CISO review, and an explicit step-by-step pilot-to-production runbook.

Use: field sellers, solutions engineers, and deal desk for pilots where customers must minimize legal/security friction and prove CPI (cost-per-inference) before committing to Dedicated or Private deployments.

Positioning: the 90-second narrative
----------------------------------
- Problem: regulated teams need predictable inference economics, provable data controls, and operational SLAs but lack time or expertise to build a production inference stack.
- Redwood answer (one sentence): Redwood provides a single inference runtime and control plane that delivers predictable latency, clear per-token economics, and turnkey private deployment options so regulated teams can pilot quickly and graduate to SLA-backed capacity without re-architecting.
- Why it matters: lowers procurement friction (security + cost evidence), shortens pilot to production, reduces vendor risk via fallbacks and observable regressions.

Top-line messaging (talking points for sales engineers)
-----------------------------------------------------
- Predictability and control: measurable SLOs (p99 < 120ms for typical conv workloads) and per-route cost reporting in Redwood Console.
- Separation of concerns: choose Hosted for fast pilots, Dedicated for committed throughput, Private (VPC or on-prem) for data residency and compliance.
- Cost-first optimizations: Redwood Optimize recommends batching/quantization with expected CPU/GPU unit economics and shows delta vs baseline in pilot dashboards.
- Guardrail-first quality: built-in evals and regression alerts tied to your reference prompts to prevent silent quality regressions during model or kernel upgrades.

Competitive brief (short)
-------------------------
- Incumbent managed LLM APIs: faster to start but opaque economics and limited private deployment; strength: broad model catalog and rapid time-to-market. Redwood differentiator: transparent per-request economics, deterministic routing and private deployment options.
- Hyperscaler endpoints (self-managed): strong infra control but large ops burden and longer time-to-value. Redwood differentiator: unified control plane + opinionated runtime that reduces engineering lift for inference.
- Self-hosted inference vendors/OSS runtimes: great for cost optimization at scale but require deep infra skill. Redwood differentiator: we provide optimized runtime and managed options that make quantization and batching safe for regulated customers.

Pitch deck one-page outline (slide titles + bullets)
--------------------------------------------------
1) Problem: "We need predictable inference for regulated workloads" — concrete pain points (cost surprises, audits, model drift).
2) Solution: Redwood snapshot (Runtime + Console + Dedicated/Private) — three lines showing the flow: dev -> pilot -> scale.
3) Pilot scope: sample integration (API keys, allowed IPs, sample prompt set, 2-week objectives).
4) Economics: pilot pricing summary and projected unit economics at 1M tokens/day (see pricing table).
5) Security & compliance: top controls included in pilot and escalation path for confidential data.
6) Success criteria & handoff: performance thresholds, quality gates, and timeline to Dedicated/Private.

Pilot pricing guidance (templates and assumptions)
------------------------------------------------
- Objective: remove pricing ambiguity for pilots while providing pathways to predictable committed pricing.
- Pilot terms (recommended default): 30-day pilot, up to 5M tokens, hosted environment with limited IP allowlist, audit logging enabled. Fixed pilot fee: $4,500 (covers 5M tokens and entitlement to a single Dedicated sizing recommendation). Overage: $0.0008 per additional token.
- Pilot-to-commit conversion discounts (illustrative): commit to Dedicated (6–12 month) and receive a 30–45% discount on per-token hosted-equivalent cost plus waived onboarding credits.

Pricing scenario table (plain-text)
----------------------------------
| Scenario | Pilot (30d) | Equivalent Monthly at 1M tokens/day | Notes |
| Pilot fixed fee | $4,500 | — | includes Console dashboards, basic evals, single custom prompt set |
| Host per-token (baseline) | $0.0009 | $27,000 | 1M tokens/day ~ 30M/month |
| Dedicated estimate (committed) | N/A | $16,500 | ~40% cost reduction vs hosted baseline with SLA |

Representative anonymized case studies
--------------------------------------
1) FinTech fraud-review pilot (Mid-market, US).
   - Ask: low-latency scoring for transaction triage, data residency controls, audit logs for model inputs.
   - Setup: 14-day Hosted pilot, IP-restricted endpoints, prompt-level evals.
   - Outcomes: Achieved p99 latency 110ms, reduced triage manual review by 48%, and converted to Dedicated after pilot; estimated savings 36% per inference vs prior hosted provider.

2) Health SaaS summarization trial (Enterprise, EMEA).
   - Ask: on-prem inference for PHI, deterministic model rollback, and integration with customer KMS.
   - Setup: Hybrid pilot (Private control plane + on-prem model runtime), 30-day coexistence with legacy pipeline.
   - Outcomes: Passed security assessment in 18 days, integrated HSM-backed keys, and moved to a Private deployment with annual license.

Security & procurement FAQ (targeted answers for CISO/Legal)
------------------------------------------------------------
Q: Can you support data residency and air-gapped deployments?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. Our Private control plane can be configured to never persist customer inputs in our hosted telemetry.

Q: How is data encrypted at rest and in transit?
A: TLS 1.2+ in transit. At rest, we integrate with KMS/HSM providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and external HSMs for Private). Audit logs include key rotation events.

Q: What logs are available during pilots?
A: Token-level usage, per-request latency, model version, prompt hash (optional), and evaluation result metrics. Raw customer payload logging is optional and can be disabled by policy.

Q: How do you manage model updates or rollbacks?
A: Rollouts are controlled via per-route versioning and canary policies. The Console shows model diff metrics; automatic rollback triggers exist for regression alerts tied to customer-defined prompt sets.

Q: What compliance attestations do you provide?
A: Redwood provides SOC2 Type II and ongoing mappings for ISO/IEC controls. For high-compliance pilots we provide an evidence package and assist with vendor assessments.

Playbook: pilot runbook (2-week technical checklist)
---------------------------------------------------
1) Pre-engagement (Days -7 to 0): legal noodle — handshake on NDA and pilot SOW; procurement to confirm IP allowlist and required attestations.
2) Day 0: onboarding: provide API key, white-listed IPs, and sample prompt set; enable audit logging; SRE/SE kickoff call.
3) Days 1–3: integration: customer integrates with Redwood API; run smoke tests; collect baseline latency and token counts. Command examples:
   - curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"<sample>"}'
4) Days 4–10: evaluation: run defined prompt set against candidate models; enable Redwood Optimize suggestions; capture cost delta for batching/quantization.
5) Days 11–14: review & convert: present results (latency, cost, quality), recommended Dedicated sizing or Private packaging, and proposed commercial terms.

Success criteria (example gates to convert)
------------------------------------------
- Performance: p95 latency <= 80% of baseline SLA stated in pilot SOW.
- Quality: automated eval set passes target accuracy threshold (customer-defined).
- Economics: projected per-inference cost within agreed threshold vs their target (e.g., <= 0.6x current baseline).
- Security: required attestations and controls validated by security review (within agreed timeframe).

Appendix: artifacts to deliver in pilot handoff
----------------------------------------------
- Pilot summary deck (1 pager): integration notes, eval metrics, cost projection.
- Dedicated sizing recommendation (CSV): estimated GPUs, concurrency targets, and autoscale policy suggestion.
- Security evidence bundle: SOC2 snapshot, encryption/KMS config, audit-log sample (redacted).

Next steps (checklist for seller)
--------------------------------
- [ ] Confirm pilot scope with procurement and security champions.
- [ ] Lock pilot SOW and signature (NDA + 30-day pilot terms).
- [ ] Schedule SE kickoff and SRE on-call windows.
- [ ] Deliver pilot summary within 48 hours of pilot completion and present conversion options.

End of document.
